question: How do consonants depend on vowels and what is the root of the phoneme stream?
premises: A consonant arises through connection with manifestation.
Consonants have vowels as their life-breath.
In the stream of phonemes, the root is only the group of six vowels.
inference: Consonants are dependent manifestations, while a sixfold set of vowels is the living root of all phonemic emanation.
uncertainties: The identity of the 'six' vowels follows a specific Tantric phonemic scheme not fully spelled out here.
plain_english: A consonant becomes manifest through articulation, but its life-breath is the vowel; indeed, in the whole stream of phonemes, the root is only the group of six vowels.
